title: Keyboard Manager new interface exits unexpectedly.

judgment.rationale: The logs and later discussion line up with the WinUI 3 Keyboard Manager editor launch-crash family that PR #49524 fixed by making the editor self-contained.
evidence: The issue says the new Keyboard Manager UI process appears and exits without showing a window.
A maintainer comment quotes errors loading Powertoys.KeyboardManagerEditorLibraryWrapper.dll and failing to initialize the mapping service.
Later commenters describe missing Windows App Runtime components or the same editor-open failure family.

Merged PR #49524 explicitly fixes the WinUI 3 Keyboard Manager editor launch crash by building the editor self-contained, and related issue #49399 was later confirmed fixed on a prerelease containing that change.
judgment.recommended_action: Route this issue to the existing self-contained editor fix path and revalidate on a current build instead of opening a second Keyboard Manager startup investigation.

fix_assessment.rationale: A concrete upstream fix already exists for this editor-startup failure family.

issue_context.summary: The new Keyboard Manager editor exits during startup. Public logs and later Windows App Runtime symptoms match the WinUI 3 startup-crash family already addressed by PR #49524.
known_information: The report targets PowerToys 0.100.2 on Windows 10 and says PowerToys.KeyboardManagerUI.exe appears and immediately exits.
A maintainer comment already extracted dependency-loading failures from the uploaded logs.
Later commenters report a missing Windows App Runtime prompt or the same failure to open the editor.
A related issue (#49399) later received public confirmation that a prerelease build resolved the same launch-crash family.
inferences: The observed problem lives in the WinUI 3 editor startup/dependency path, not in remap execution after the editor launches.
Because a merged self-contained packaging fix already exists, new standalone design work here would duplicate resolved upstream work.
issue_context.analysis: This issue has a strong existing-fix signal. The lightweight dashboard outcome is to keep it with the self-contained editor fix path and not spend additional batch capacity on a fresh design. The only remaining public question is whether current builds containing PR #49524 fully clear the symptom for these reporters.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the issue body, all public comments, and the current live labels.
Reviewed the previously generated artifact and confirmed it was stale because it predated the newest public comment on 2026-09-09.
Reviewed PR #49524 and related issue #49399 to confirm they target the same WinUI 3 Keyboard Manager editor startup crash family.
Reviewed the previously inspected public bug-report evidence documenting missing editor dependencies.
